sections.content:
44,835 people

were counted on the census as "groundworkers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Groundworkers prepare construction sites for building work by digging out and levelling the ground and laying concrete foundations, installing pipes and drainage and building paths, roads and driveways.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "groundworkers" there were more men than women (99.2% compared with 0.8%).

This means "groundworkers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary trades and related occupations".

Men made up 99.2% and women made up 0.8% of "groundworkers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "groundworkers" included:

  • bricklayers
  • roofers, roof tilers and slaters
  • scaffolders, stagers and riggers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "groundworkers", 16.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "groundworkers" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "groundworkers" included:

  • buyers and procurement officers
  • agricultural and fishing trades (other)
  • air-conditioning and refrigeration installers and repairers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "groundworkers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "groundworkers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "groundworkers", 6.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93.3% compared with 6.7%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (61.3%) than an employee (38.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included West Northamptonshire, this is in the region of the East Midlands.
